title: Agent-led rookie tutorial
details: Completed: Claude or Codex guides students through Create, Build, Practice, and Compete in chat. Students choose their bot's name and strategy, can watch training highlights, and approve changes and submissions. No website onboarding wizard is required.

previous_title: A simpler, game-like My Bot home
title: Give My Bot one clear next action
details: Already available: a focused My Bot page with a character, bot identity, current status, Elo, and rank. Remaining: show one useful next action for each state, such as creating a first bot, reviewing a result, or returning to the coding agent to train. Keep the page calm and avoid extra dashboard panels.

title: Add evidence-based questions after a recap
details: Already available: animated website and local hand replays, chronological highlights, individual-hand selection, face-up cards, chip movement, and playback controls. Remaining: end a recap with specific questions tied to the recorded hands so students can form a hypothesis and prompt their coding agent. Students choose strategy changes; there is no automatic Improve my bot button.

previous_title: Hosted training missions against strategy bots
title: 5 Packaged Training Bots
details: Offer five ready-to-play practice opponents with distinct strategies and difficulty levels. Students can ask Claude or Codex to choose an opponent and run training over the existing WebSocket, then review the hands in the recap viewer. Track which bots a student has beaten and let their coding agent suggest the next opponent. Practice uses play chips and does not change public Elo.

title: Match Sharing Cards
details: Generate polished share images and suggested text for a great match or hand, but require the student to review and share it themselves. Alpha Poker should never post automatically.

previous_title: Private XP and season progress on profiles
title: Gamify: Private XP and season progress on profiles
details: Show optional private XP, a level, and compact season progress on the student profile while keeping public Elo as the measure of bot strength. Reward learning and experimentation, cap repetitive grinding, and avoid purchases, loot boxes, or streak pressure.
